description:
FOUND s465ba (Opus, round 23) while shipping #1032, and it is the RESIDUE
that fix deliberately left.  PRE-EXISTING for `close`/`eof`/`fileno`; for
`stat`/`lstat` #1032 turned it from a CRASH into this wrong answer, which is
the family's own long-standing answer rather than a new shape.

PERL (probed 5.40.3, scratch/p13-const-handle-slot.pl):

    use constant CPATH => '/etc/passwd';
    sub SPATH { '/etc/passwd' }
    print scalar(stat(SPATH)), "\n";     # 1   -- the sub is CALLED
    print scalar(stat(CPATH)), "\n";     # 1
    print -e SPATH ? 1 : 0, "\n";        # 1
    eof(CPATH);                          # calls CPATH, then uses the RESULT
                                         # as a handle name (perl's warning
                                         # says "on unopened filehandle
                                         # /etc/passwd", which proves it)

PCL's EMISSION shows exactly where the two paths part company:

    -e SPATH        ->  (p--e (pl-SPATH))                  CORRECT
    -e CPATH        ->  (p--e (p-scalar-ctx (pl-CPATH)))   CORRECT
    stat(SPATH)     ->  (p-stat SPATH)                     the bare word
    stat(CPATH)     ->  (p-stat CPATH)                     the bare word
    eof(CPATH)      ->  (p-eof CPATH)                      the bare word
    close(CPATH)    ->  (p-close CPATH)                    the bare word

So the FILETEST OPERAND path asks the bareword classifier
(`_bareword_callable_here`, #266's three-valued predicate) and the
PAREN-ARGUMENT path does not: it hands the word through and lets the
runtime's `%p-fh-arg` macro quote it as a handle name.

POPULATION, MEASURED (scratch/scan-stat-bareword.pl over perl-tests/, lib/,
Pl/t/, cpan-tests/, examples/ and perl's own t/ = 1452 files, 2412 bareword
operand slots): the shape occurs ZERO times.  The scanner's 33 hits are all
either `_` (the stat-cache variable, which #1032 excludes by name) or a
bareword inside a STRING LITERAL in a test description.  That is why #1032
shipped without it -- the residue costs no measurable row, in any population.

FIX SHAPE (untried): ask `_bareword_callable_here` in the paren-argument
path too, so a callable bareword becomes `(pl-NAME)` and a non-callable one
stays bare for `%p-fh-arg` to quote.  ONE predicate for both paths (rule 11).
DO NOT do it by widening `%p-fh-arg`'s `(pl-NAME)` arm instead: `open`'s
first argument is a GLOB slot, not a read slot, and perl does NOT call a
declared sub there -- so a runtime-side rule would have to distinguish the
two slots anyway, which is the distinction the compiler already has.

CAUTION named by #1032's own note: the filetest operand path must keep
emitting the CALL.  `%p-fh-arg`'s `(pl-NAME)` arm is switched OFF for the
stat/filetest family precisely so that `(p--e (pl-SPATH))` is not turned back
into a handle name; guard rows 21-23 of `Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t` assert
that, and they must stay green through this fix.

=== ADDENDUM (s465ba, same session): THE RULE IS TWO GROUPS, AND ir-spec 7.5
WAS WRONG ABOUT IT ===

Re-measured with the warning TEXT as the discriminator, which is the only
thing that tells "the bareword went into the glob slot" from "the sub was
called and its RESULT used as a handle name" -- `tell` answers -1 either way
(scratch/p17-builtin-slot-rule.pl + scratch/p18-slot-warning-names.pl,
perl 5.40.3):

    sub FILE1 () { 42 }
    sub SPATH    { 'ZZPATH' }
    use constant CPATH => 'YYPATH';

    tell FILE1     ->  "tell() on unopened filehandle 42"      the sub RAN
    tell SPATH     ->  "tell() on unopened filehandle "        it did NOT
    tell CPATH     ->  "tell() on unopened filehandle YYPATH"  it RAN
    close(CPATH)   ->  "close() on unopened filehandle YYPATH" it RAN
    -e SPATH  = 1,  stat SPATH  = 13 elements                  it RAN
    -e FILE1  = 0,  stat FILE1  = 0  elements   (there is no file "42")

So there are THREE rules, not one:

  (a) a `()`-PROTOTYPE sub -- `use constant` included -- is INLINED by the
      parser before any slot sees it, in EVERY one of these builtins.  That
      is what makes ir-spec's own example (`sub FILE1 () {42}; tell FILE1`
      is -1) true for the wrong reason: the handle is named "42".
  (b) an ordinary sub in a GLOB slot (`tell eof fileno close binmode seek`,
      the `open` family) does NOT displace the bareword -- the handle wins.
  (c) an ordinary sub in an EXPR slot (`stat lstat -X`) IS called.

ir-spec 7.5 asserted (b) for all of them and was corrected in the #1032
commit.  This task therefore has a SHARPER scope than "ask the classifier in
the paren-arg path": the classifier must be asked for the EXPR slots (c), and
the `()`-prototype inline (a) is a SEPARATE question that applies to the glob
slots too -- `close(CPATH)` is wrong today in the same way `stat(CPATH)` is,
and the constants table (`Pl::Environment`) already knows which names are
inlinable.  Measure (a)'s population before taking it: `use constant` names
in a handle slot may be commoner than declared subs there.

=== DONE (s470bx, 2026-09-06) ===

CLOSED with #1231 â they are one predicate seen from two sides, and the
addendum's sharper scope is what shipped: the classifier is asked for the EXPR
slots (rule (c)), the GLOB slots keep the handle (rule (b)), and the fix is
keyed on WHICH BUILTIN, as a `expr_slot => 1` flag on `stat` and `lstat` in
`Pl::Environment::_builtin_prototypes`.  `_read_star_slot_bareword`'s builtin
half consumes it generically; nothing in `Pl/` or `cl/` names a module.

The task's own population measurement stood up: the PAREN spelling
`stat(SPATH)` occurs nowhere, and the emission A/B over lib + perl's own t/ +
cpan-tests (1035 files) shows NO file changing because of this â the diffs are
#1043's context wrap and nothing else.  The rows came from the PAREN-LESS
spelling inside a string eval (`t/op/stat_errors.t`), which is #1231's half.

MEASURED vs perl 5.40.3 after the fix (scratch/s470bx/p1231.pl, 22 rows, and
p1231c.pl, 12 more through `eval ""`): `stat SPATH` and `stat CPATH` are 13
elements, `-e SPATH` and `-e CPATH` are 1, and every undeclared bareword is
EBADF â identical to perl in both the file and the eval horizon.

NOT DONE, and it is the addendum's rule (a): the `()`-PROTOTYPE inline in a
GLOB slot.  `close(CPATH)` and `tell CPATH` still pass the bareword where perl
calls the constant first and uses its RESULT as the handle name.  The
addendum's instruction â measure (a)'s population before taking it â is
unchanged and untaken here; it is a separate change to the glob-slot half,
which this one deliberately did not touch.  Filed as #1291.
subject: DIVERGENCE (pre-existing, whole family): a BAREWORD argument to a handle-taking builtin -- `stat(X)`, `close(X)`, `eof(X)`, `fileno(X)` -- is read as a handle NAME even when a sub or constant X is declared, where perl CALLS it.  `use constant CPATH => '/etc/passwd'; stat(CPATH)` is 13 elements in perl and 0 here.  The FILETEST spelling `-e CPATH` is already right, so the compiler HAS the classifier -- it just is not asked in the paren-argument path.
